name: DocPrompting / RepoCoder - Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors_affiliation: DocPrompting: Shuyan Zhou, Uri Alon, Frank F. Xu, Zhiruo Wang, Zhengbao Jiang, Graham Neubig (Language Technologies Institute, Carnegie Mellon University; Inspired Cognition). RepoCoder: Fengji Zhang, Bei Chen, Yue Zhang, Jacky Keung, Jin Liu, Daoguang Zan, Yi Mao, Jian-Guang Lou, Weizhu Chen (City University of Hong Kong; Microsoft Corporation; Wuhan University).
paper_url: DocPrompting: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05987 (ICLR 2023, OpenReview ZTCxT2t2Ru). RepoCoder: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12570 (EMNLP 2023, DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2303.12570).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (per-paper code repos only; no maintained leaderboard list).
task_domain: code (NL-to-code generation and repository-level code completion).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, supervised code generation grounded by retrieval, with no multi-agent interaction. DocPrompting: natural-language-intent-to-code generation across PLs (Python, Bash) where the model must generalize to libraries/functions and arguments unseen in training by reading retrieved documentation from an external, updatable documentation pool; the retriever is trained with supervision (oracle docs per example) plus weak supervision, and the generator is finetuned (or few-shot for Codex). RepoCoder: repository-level code completion (continue unfinished in-file code) where useful context is scattered across other files of the same repo; an iterative retrieve-then-generate loop uses the model's own previous prediction to re-query the repo. Both keep retriever and generator parameters frozen at inference (RepoCoder fully frozen; DocPrompting trains components offline).
what_is_retrieved: DocPrompting: documentation pieces (per-function / per-library / per-argument doc paragraphs from manuals or DevDocs). RepoCoder: code snippets (fixed-size sliding-window contiguous line spans extracted from other files in the same repository).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus in both. DocPrompting: an external, frequently-updatable documentation pool D (treated as static at inference, can be swapped with new-library docs without retraining). RepoCoder: the target repository's own files indexed as a static (per-repository) snapshot; the retrieval database is rebuilt per repository but is not a growing episodic agent memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking in both. DocPrompting selects top-k docs (default k=10) by similarity. RepoCoder selects up to K (=10) most-similar snippets filling the available prompt budget. Neither targets minimal-complete-set recovery nor precision-driven variable-size selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve=yes; Reuse=yes (retrieved docs/snippets injected and conditioned on); Revise=no (no case adaptation/revision step); Retain=no (no write-back of new cases). [Retrieve, Reuse] only.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - neither work frames itself as case-based reasoning nor cites Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; both are framed as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for code.
retrieval_unit: DocPrompting: document (single doc per function/library/argument; in tldr a two-level scheme - first retrieve a whole Bash manual, then top-10 paragraphs within it). RepoCoder: token/snippet - a fixed-size code snippet of contiguous lines defined by sliding-window size Sw with stride Ss.
index_source: Static, offline-constructed store in both. DocPrompting: a global documentation pool shared across all examples (tldr ~400k paragraphs from 1,879 Bash manuals; CoNaLa 35,763 function docs from DevDocs). RepoCoder: a per-repository retrieval database built offline by sliding-window partitioning of repo files (no online/test-time growth).
index_structure_topology: DocPrompting: flat similarity index over documents (in tldr a 2-level hierarchy: manual -> paragraph). RepoCoder: flat index of sliding-window code snippets (bag-of-words / dense vectors), keyed by file path; no dependency/knowledge graph.
retriever_type: DocPrompting: both sparse (Elasticsearch BM25) and dense (contrastively-trained dense retriever initialized from SimCSE/RoBERTa or CodeT5-base encoder); BM25 best on tldr, CodeT5 dense best on CoNaLa. RepoCoder: main experiments use a sparse bag-of-words retriever scored by Jaccard index over token sets; also tested a dense UniXcoder retriever (equivalent performance).
retriever_learning_signal: DocPrompting: dense retriever trained with contrastive loss on similarity labels (oracle docs as positives, in-batch negatives) MIXED with weak self-supervision (SimCSE-style dropout-masked sentence pairs over the doc pool); sparse BM25 is off-the-shelf (none). RepoCoder: none - the similarity-based retriever (Jaccard/UniXcoder) is fixed/off-the-shelf with no training; learning signal is absent (parameters of R and M unchanged throughout).
query_construction: DocPrompting: raw NL intent n used directly as the query. RepoCoder: iteration 1 uses the last (Sw-Ss) lines of the unfinished in-file code X; iteration i>1 augments the query by concatenating those last (Sw-Ss) lines of X with the first Ss lines of the model's previous prediction Y_hat^{i-1} (self-generated query expansion / pseudo-completion).
query_granularity: DocPrompting: task-level (one-shot at t=0 from the intent). RepoCoder: trajectory/step-level via iteration - the completion position query is re-formed each iteration using the latest generated draft.
when_to_retrieve: DocPrompting: one-shot (single retrieval before generation). RepoCoder: iterative (fixed number of retrieval-generation iterations; 2 iterations is the recommended/best setting, with the prior prediction grounding the next retrieval).
retrieval_trigger_signal: DocPrompting: fixed schedule (retrieve once before generating). RepoCoder: fixed schedule / fixed iteration count - retrieval re-triggered each iteration deterministically; no confidence/uncertainty/learned trigger.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage in either. DocPrompting takes top-k by retriever similarity. RepoCoder orders retrieved snippets in ascending similarity within the prompt but applies no separate reranker (cross-encoder/RRF).
retrieved_context_refinement: Largely none. DocPrompting: top-k docs concatenated (with FiD encoding each (intent, doc) pair separately for T5/CodeT5 to fit length). RepoCoder: snippets concatenated with file-path headers up to a token budget (retrieved content set to half the prompt length); no decompose/distill/compression beyond truncation to budget.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill descriptions). DocPrompting indexes raw documentation paragraphs / function docs as-is (oracle docs built via string/function-name matching for training supervision, not as runtime augmentation).
index_content_separation: DocPrompting (tldr) uses a coarse-to-fine separation: a lightweight manual-level index retrieved first, then paragraph-level content within the top manual. Otherwise no progressive-disclosure / index-then-content split.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - no live tool index or integration protocol (no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling). DocPrompting's doc pool is described as updatable with new-library docs but is not auto-synced.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation in both. DocPrompting: retrieved docs concatenated with the NL intent as the generator prompt (or FiD fusion in the decoder); generator finetuned to maximize p(code | intent, docs) (few-shot ICL for Codex). RepoCoder: retrieved code snippets prepended (with originating file paths) to the unfinished code in a prompt template; the frozen code LM completes the code.
planning_integration: DocPrompting: retrieve-then-generate (one-shot exemplars/docs at generation time). RepoCoder: iterative retrieve-then-generate loop where each generated draft conditions the next retrieval (generate-then-retrieve-then-regenerate); no MCTS/tree search and no explicit planner.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: DocPrompting: per-answer (single retrieval, single generation). RepoCoder: per-iteration / per-draft-completion - retrieval interleaved at the granularity of whole completion attempts (each iteration produces a full candidate completion that re-grounds retrieval).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A for DocPrompting (no case adaptation). RepoCoder's iterative loop functions as an execution-free, prediction-driven query refinement rather than a CBR case-revision step.
retrieved_item_representation: DocPrompting: raw natural-language documentation text (function/argument descriptions) injected into the prompt. RepoCoder: raw code snippets (verbatim line spans) with file-path comments injected into the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: DocPrompting: documentation/manual (descriptive reference text, more abstract than code) - a hint/usage description. RepoCoder: raw code (single demonstration-like snippet of concrete repo code).
noise_robustness_mechanism: DocPrompting: retriever finetuned on the target programming language plus weak supervision improves doc relevance (better alignment reduces noise); generator finetuned to condition on retrieved docs. RepoCoder: relies on similarity-based filtering and iterative re-grounding (using the generated draft to fetch more on-target snippets) plus ascending-similarity ordering; no explicit relevance evaluator or distractor-aware training.
memory_type: none - no persistent episodic/skill/workflow memory. DocPrompting uses a static external doc pool; RepoCoder uses a per-repository static snippet index. Neither maintains an evolving agent memory.
write_back: False - neither stores new experiences/cases/skills back into a memory store. RepoCoder's previous prediction is used transiently as the next query, not persisted.
online_growth: False - retrievable stores are frozen after offline construction; they do not grow during deployment. (DocPrompting's doc pool can be manually updated with new docs but does not self-grow at test time.)
write_back_trigger: never - no write-back event in either system.
failure_experience_usage: Not used as stored experience. RepoCoder reuses its own (possibly incorrect) intermediate prediction only as a query-expansion signal within the same instance loop; failed completions are not stored or contrastively retrieved.
memory_evolution_update: N/A - no stored entries are mutated (no memory). RepoCoder's transient query is regenerated, not an evolving memory record.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No - retrieval/selection is fixed similarity top-k (BM25/dense/Jaccard), not an RL/learned selection policy. (DocPrompting trains the dense retriever's representations contrastively, but selection remains fixed top-k; no policy over when/what to retrieve.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No - single-model pipelines; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: DocPrompting: tldr (new Bash NL-to-command benchmark, 1,879 unique commands / 9,187 NL-Bash pairs, train/dev/test with disjoint commands; doc pool ~400k paragraphs) and a new re-split of CoNaLa (Python; 2,135/201/543 train/dev/test, doc pool 35,763 DevDocs function docs; +100 examples with manual unit tests for pass@k). RepoCoder: RepoEval (new benchmark, latest GitHub repos created after 2022-01-01, >100 stars, >80% Python, with unit tests; three granularities: line completion 1,600 samples, API invocation completion 1,600 samples, function body completion 373 samples with unit-test execution).
benchmark_family: code (NL-to-code generation: CoNaLa, tldr; repository-level code completion: RepoEval, related to RepoEval/CrossCodeEval family). Not QA/web/embodied/tool.
baselines: DocPrompting: base generators without retrieval (GPT-Neo-125M, GPT-Neo-1.3B, T5-base, CodeT5-base, Codex code-davinci-001 3-shot); ExPrompting (retrieving NL-code pairs/examples instead of docs, following Parvez et al. 2021 / Pasupat et al. 2021); oracle-docs and oracle-command-name upper bounds; multiple retrievers (BM25, RoBERTa off-shelf/finetuned, CodeT5 off-shelf/finetuned). RepoCoder: In-File completion (no retrieval), vanilla single-iteration RAG, and an Oracle method (single retrieval using the ground-truth completion as query, an upper bound); also GT-Code (static-analysis-located ground-truth-API snippets) in analysis; generators GPT-3.5-Turbo, CODEGEN-Mono 6B/2B/350M.
key_metrics: DocPrompting: pass@k (execution), exact match (EM), token-level F1, character-level BLEU / BLEU-4, command-name accuracy (CMD Acc), function-name recall and unseen-function recall; retrieval recall@k. RepoCoder: Exact Match (EM), Edit Similarity (ES), unit-test Pass Rate (PR) for function bodies, and retrieval Recall (fraction of retrieved snippets containing ground-truth API invocations).
headline_result: DocPrompting: improves CodeT5 by +2.85% pass@1 (52% relative gain) and +4.39% pass@10 (30% relative) in execution-based eval on CoNaLa; up to +6.9% absolute EM on tldr for CodeT5/GPT-Neo-1.3B. RepoCoder: improves the In-File completion baseline by over 10% EM across all settings on RepoEval and consistently beats vanilla RAG; e.g. ICSE'25 RLCoder reports RepoCoder as a strong baseline and RepoCoder claims >8% absolute ES and >10% absolute EM gains over In-File.
ablations: DocPrompting: (1) retriever comparison (Table 4) - BM25 matches dense retrievers on tldr but is far weaker on CoNaLa (recall@10 9.73% vs CodeT5 55.81%), showing dataset-dependent retriever choice; (2) PL-pretrained retrievers (CodeT5 on Python) beat text-pretrained (RoBERTa); (3) mixing supervised + weak (SimCSE-style) supervision improves the retriever vs supervised-only; (4) docs-vs-examples: DocPrompting >> ExPrompting; (5) oracle-docs and oracle-command-name give large additional gains (e.g. Codex EM 22.44%->32.43% with oracle command). RepoCoder: (1) number of iterations - 2 iterations consistently beat 1-iteration vanilla RAG, with Recall of ground-truth-API snippets rising (e.g. GPT-3.5-Turbo API recall 86.04%->90.34% from iter1->iter2); (2) sparse Jaccard vs dense UniXcoder retriever - roughly equivalent (robustness); (3) restricting retrieval to specific file locations degrades performance; (4) GT-Code/Oracle upper bounds show retrieval quality drives completion accuracy.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes - both report intrinsic retrieval metrics separately from end-to-end task metrics. DocPrompting reports retrieval recall@k (Table 4) independent of generation quality. RepoCoder reports retrieval Recall (ground-truth-API snippet recall) alongside EM/ES.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-focused (final code correctness: pass@k/EM/ES/PR), but both add a process-quality lens via retrieval recall (whether the needed doc/snippet was retrieved), and RepoCoder analyzes per-iteration recall improvement.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: DocPrompting: minimal added cost - single retrieval pass; FiD used to fit multiple docs within length limits; few-shot (3-shot) for Codex. RepoCoder: extra cost from iterative generation+retrieval (multiple LM calls per completion); paper notes 2 iterations gives best accuracy/cost balance and that performance is not highly sensitive to hyper-parameters; CODEGEN-350M+RepoCoder approaches GPT-3.5-Turbo In-File, implying a cost-quality lever. No explicit latency/$ numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: DocPrompting: top-k = 10 retrieved docs (default) used in all main results; FiD encodes docs separately to handle T5/CodeT5 512-token limit. RepoCoder: prompt budget 4,096 tokens (GPT-3.5-Turbo) / 2,048 (CODEGEN); retrieved snippets capped at half the prompt length; max K=10 snippets; sliding window Sw=20, stride Ss=10 (line/API), Sw=50/Ss=10 (function body); max generated tokens 100 (line/API) / 500 (function).
benchmark_construction_and_size: DocPrompting tldr: human-written NL intents from community tldr pages, 1,879 commands / 9,187 pairs, disjoint-command splits, oracle docs via string matching, doc pool ~400k paragraphs. DocPrompting CoNaLa: re-split of StackOverflow-mined pairs (2,135/201/543) guaranteeing >=1 unseen function per dev/test example, doc pool 35,763 DevDocs function docs, 100 manually-unit-tested examples for execution eval. RepoCoder RepoEval: reverse-engineered from real GitHub repos created after 2022-01-01 (avoid leakage), >100 stars, >80% Python, with unit tests; line (1,600), API invocation (1,600), function body (373, unit-test verifiable). Answer verifiability: similarity-based (EM/ES) for line/API, execution-based (unit-test Pass Rate) for function body.
builds_on: Retrieval-augmented generation / retrieval-conditioned generation (Lewis et al. RAG; REALM; Fusion-in-Decoder, Izacard & Grave 2021); dense retrieval (DPR Karpukhin et al., SimCSE Gao et al.) and BM25; code LMs (CodeT5, GPT-Neo, Codex, CODEGEN, UniXcoder, GPT-3.5-Turbo). RepoCoder builds on similarity-based code retrieval (Lu et al. ReACC 2022) and the In-File completion paradigm; query-shifting idea from Lu et al. 2022. DocPrompting builds on NL-to-code generation (CoNaLa, Yin et al.).
contrasts_with: DocPrompting contrasts with example/snippet-retrieval methods (ExPrompting; Parvez et al. 2021 REDCODER; Pasupat et al. 2021) by retrieving documentation instead of NL-code examples, and with parametric-only code LMs that cannot generalize to unseen libraries/functions. RepoCoder contrasts with: In-File-only completion; single-pass vanilla RAG for code; static-analysis/heuristic completion (Raychev et al.; Svyatkovskiy et al.) and classifier-based prompt construction (Shrivastava et al. RLPG 2022, Repository-Level Prompt Generation) by being training-free and iterative.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task-solving): static-corpus retrieval-augmented code generation. DocPrompting = documentation-grounded one-shot retrieve-then-generate (lineage of doc/knowledge-grounded code LMs). RepoCoder = iterative self-grounded retrieval-generation for repository context (lineage of iterative RAG and repository-level code completion, predecessor to RLCoder, CrossCodeEval, and repo-level agentic code methods).
